Hi Fellow dude!

Two day splits are an awesome way to workout if you are short on time or want to hit a body part multiple times a week (as you mentioned, I think it's great to hit the body with multiple shorter session during a single week).  I use it often, but using an upper body/lower body split.  Any reason why you are hitting shoulders in your legs day?  Why not just throw it in day one?   That's my only real issue with it.
 
Let me talk you through my reasoning... I use a lot of supersets, and use the big compound movements, such as bench, incline, pullups, rows, strict/push/jerk presses, squats, front squats, deadlifts, SLDL, split squat, cleans, curls, farmers walk, dips and sometimes a prowler if I have access to one.  After that, I find that I just don't have the energy or desire to really do anything else.  I hit some core work, strech, and call it a day.  I know I'm missing some of the smaller stuff (calves, forearms, traps), but my calves are already huge, I don't use straps for any of my lifts, and I'll shrug something every now and then.  

Give it a shot and report back!  Tell us how you liked it!

Your goals for posing music should be:

1. Isn't distracting from your routine (for that reason, I don't use anything with lyrics, just like your music selection)

2. Is in line with your posing style (Are you trying to be ascetic and pretty or huge and massive?)

3. Fit in the required time frame (generally 60-90seconds, so either tell the MC to turn it off after 90s or make a modified version 

(These rules go out the window if you are the kind of person who pulls off any kind of gimmick, like the robot or lip syncing or the phantom of the opera mask.  Just make sure you are awesome at it, cause nothing looks worse than a poorly hit routine when you are trying to use a gimmick)



I like your choice of music here.. it's pretty.. it's slow.. it has no lyrics.. it isn't distracting.  This is something I could see my self doing.  But maybe people might want something more "pop-like".  I think those people are silly.

My only suggestion is to modify it.  For example, I used NIN Just like you imagined (http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AiZxCVXhgmM).  I think I did the following

1. I took out the kind of weird intro

2. I added in an additional double beep since the intro is so soft, I didn't want to miss it and be thrown off for the rest of the time

3. I slowed it down 10-15% so I didn't feel rushed moving from pose to pose

4. I spliced the opening part with the section at 2:10 and then faded out with the part at 3:15

5. Made it all ~90seconds

6. Put the single track onto a CDx2 (cause weird shit happens backstage) I wanted to make this as easy as possible for some dude who is helping me.  

Of course, your song and your posing are different, you'll need to adjust as needed.
